fields.v: Success criterion: no criterion stated by the authors (SASR/DASR on BigCodeBench reported; cost not measured for any configuration). (1) PackHallu + OpenHands + 5 backbones (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, Qwen3-Coder-30B, Devstral-Small-2-24B, GLM4.7-Flash-30B, Gemma4-31B), same surrogate and victim: avg SASR 79.29%, DASR 67.68% (per package SASR 70.02-86.19%, DASR >56%). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. (2) Baselines in the same settings: Combined Attack avg SASR/DASR 14.99/11.35; Repeat, GCG, ObliInjection lower; TAP strongest baseline (e.g. Qwen3-Coder-30B Pandas 34.62/26.92 vs PackHallu 98.72/89.74). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. (3) Transfer to other backbones on OpenHands (12 LLMs incl. GPT-5.5, GPT-5.3-Codex, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Llama-4-Maverick): >90% SASR on >=3 of 5 packages for 8 of 12; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 22.73-50.00% SASR, 7.89-26.47% DASR. No criterion stated by the authors. (4) Transfer to other frameworks with Qwen3-Coder-30B (OpenCode, Aider, Pi, Cline, Kilo Code): avg SASR 71.55%, DASR 62.99%. No criterion stated by the authors. (5) Claude Code 2.1.141 + Claude Sonnet 4.6: SASR 31.03-58.95%, DASR 31.03-57.89% (most resistant). No criterion stated by the authors. (6) Cursor + Auto: SASR 69.35-98.00%; Cursor + Composer 2.5: 81.40-95.65%; OpenCode + DeepSeek-V4-Flash: 75.32-93.94%; average of the four agents in (5)-(6) SASR 74.81%, DASR 65.38%. No criterion stated by the authors. (7) Dataset transfer: DS-1000 SASR 53.33 / DASR 45.00; RefactorBench 18.60 / 16.28. No criterion stated by the authors. Ablations: injection location (OpenCode + DeepSeek-V4-Flash, stated): beginning avg SASR 82.63 vs 74.03 middle, 77.29 end; initializations (setting not stated; default row 97.50/97.50 matches OpenHands + Qwen3-Coder-30B on Seaborn in Table 2): default + 4 paraphrased prompts 98.00±2.09 SASR, 96.00±1.37 DASR; components (setting not stated; full row 83.87/50.54 matches OpenCode + DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Pandas): w/o trajectory-level signal 56.99/24.73, w/o self-attributed critique 62.37/47.31, w/o strategy proposal 63.44/46.24; hyperparameters (same setting; SASR/DASR): rounds 10/20/30 75.27/38.71, 83.87/50.54, 84.95/49.46; top-k 1/5/10 43.01/21.51, 83.87/50.54, 80.65/51.61; offspring 1/3/5 56.99/26.88, 83.87/50.54, 86.02/53.76; surrogate tasks 1/10/20 21.50/10.75, 83.87/50.54, 87.10/55.91. No criterion stated by the authors

fields.v: The authors state that PackHallu outperforms all baselines on all packages and victim agents, but Table 2 shows TAP with higher DASR on GLM4.7-Flash-30B Pandas (86.59 vs 73.17) and Numpy (65.28 vs 59.72), and a tie in SASR on Devstral-Small-2-24B Numpy (44.44 each); in every other cell PackHallu is higher. Averages stated: PackHallu 79.29/67.68 vs Combined Attack 14.99/11.35 (5.29x SASR, 5.96x DASR), the only baseline average the authors give (they call it the 'subpotimal' baseline). TAP is the strongest baseline in Table 2 (e.g. Qwen3-Coder-30B Pandas 34.62/26.92 vs PackHallu 98.72/89.74); no average or ratio is reported for it. More capable backbones more vulnerable (r=0.785 for SASR vs capability); no relation across frameworks (r=-0.186). Popular packages harder to attack (median r=-0.69 SASR, -0.60 DASR). No significance tests. Detectors (FNR/FPR): ProtectAI-DeBERTa 100%/3%; PromptGuard 46%/5%; DataSentinel 49%/16%; PromptArmor 20%/34%; PIShield 21%/11%
